\section{The Transport-Boundary Completeness Matrix}
\label{app:completeness}
% ===========================================================================

Every category--gas combination on the transport boundary, with its IPCC
notation key and the justification the engine carries. The boundary spans
four reporting codes deliberately: the diesel this sector's residual class
and unresolved claimants actually belong to sits in 1.A.2, and the vehicle
fleet's refrigerant leakage in IPPU 2.F.1. Generated from the same
completeness table the national inventory publishes, which is itself synced
to the gap register by test.

1.A.3.b & Road transport & E & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & ANCHORED ON FUEL, not on the fleet model: the OCAC FY2023-24 Road customer-class rows (petrol MS+HOBC and HSD - bulk industry, power, government and railway diesel excluded by the source's own partition), net of the household-generator petrol carve-out relayed from the residential sector, plus CNG from OGRA's metered sector gas on its own activity basis. The railway figure is an independent cross-check (Year Book FY2023-24 row vs OCAC Railways row, 3.8 percent apart), not a deduction. outputs/transport\_fuel\_ledger\_2024.csv is the executable two-tier claimant structure. KNOWN FLAW: the class split rides vehicle-kilometres, over-weighting motorcycles; the total is unaffected because it is set by the fuel rows. Retail-bought agricultural-stationary, captive and other non-road diesel remains inside the Road row (the ledger's UNRESOLVED rows), biasing 1.A.3.b high conditional on the other\ldots \\[2pt]
1.A.3.b & Electric road vehicles & NO & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & Zero direct combustion by definition, and the registered electric fleet is negligible in the 2022 registration data. Electricity-related emissions are counted at the power station in 1.A.1.a like all consumption - the Orange Line convention. Recorded so the road scope statement has a boundary row rather than an implicit omission. \\[2pt]
1.A.3.c & Railways & E & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & LOCOMOTIVE TRACTION ONLY under the re-based reference (0.38939 Mt): the Year Book detail table splits locomotive from other-than-locomotive fuel, and the measured non-traction share books at its own category row below. Pakistan Railways Year Book metered fuel consumption x IPCC Vol 2 Ch 3 Table 3.4.1, the RAIL table - its N2O factor is \\num{7.3} times the road value. Railway diesel is its own OCAC customer-class row, outside the road control by the source's structure, and the Year Book figure serves as an independent cross-check on that row (3.8 percent apart at the matched year) rather than a deduction. The mainline network has been diesel-only since about 2010 (electric energy NIL from the 2010-2015 quinquennium in the Year Book's own historical table), so there is no scope-2 stream in the inventory years; urban electric rail (Lahore Orange Line) is outside the operator, has zero dir\ldots \\[2pt]
1.A.3.a & Domestic aviation & E & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & LTO cycles from CAA movement statistics x ICAO fuel-burn tables, full-flight for domestic. International bunkers are a memo item ESTIMATED at full flight by the source-row-conserving JP-1 bridge (550,670 t of commercial JP-1, 1.740 Mt CO2, outputs/aviation\_bridge\_2024.csv); the 210.4 kt international-LTO figure is a separate local-air product, not the bunkers estimate. \\[2pt]
1.A.3.d & Water-borne navigation - domestic & NE & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & SCREENED, not estimated: the two blockers the earlier row named - a marine factor choice and a domestic/foreign boundary review - are made in sectors/transport/navigation\_screen.py, and every held OCAC edition's Domestic Bunkers row is converted in outputs/transport\_navigation\_screen\_2024.csv (3,054 t HSD in the FY2023-24 reference year, 0.0098 Mt CO2e on IPCC Tables 3.5.2/3.5.3). It stays NE for two stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the ten held editions span 32 to 8,342 t with no trend - an activity that volatile needs the port-side series before it can carry an E. See marine-domestic. \\[2pt]
1.A.4.c & Off-road machinery (tractors and plant) & E & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & Partitioned from the OCAC Road-row diesel control by the off-road share of vehicle-kilometres - the same normalisation that splits the on-road classes, so the two cannot claim the same tonne. IPCC Vol 2 Ch 3 Table 3.3.1 factors, whose N2O is \\num{7.3} times the road value (and identical between the table's Agriculture and Industry rows, so the class's mixed composition is factor-invariant under the correct table). KNOWN FLAW: the class is the source workbook's residual bucket as well as its tractor class, is modelled as 100\% diesel, and its exact share is priced by the offroad\_share scenarios. \\[2pt]
1.A.4.c & Stationary agriculture/forestry and railway workshops & IE & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & INCLUDED ELSEWHERE, not unestimated - the honest key this row carried wrong as NE: the fuel IS estimated, just in the wrong category at the wrong factors. Stationary farm plant (tube wells, threshing engines) burns diesel that remains inside the 1.A.3.b road control total and is reported there at road factors - an UNRESOLVED claimant row of outputs/transport\_fuel\_ledger\_2024.csv; OCAC publishes an agriculture row that would split it out (transport-hsd-end-use). Railway workshop, power-house, pump and track-machine fuel is MEASURED at 1,599 thousand litres (1.21 percent of the p.163 detail total) by pkinv.sectors.railways.reconcile and, since the rail re-base, reported at its own category row (1.A.2/1.A.4.c unresolved) rather than inside 1.A.3.c; the source-level split below that figure is still not published. See stationary-farm-rail-workshop and rail-yearbook-detail. \\[2pt]
1.A.2 & Captive-generation diesel and furnace oil & IE & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & Industrial self-generation liquids are IPCC 1.A.2 and are INCLUDED ELSEWHERE in two places. Bulk purchases (the channel a captive plant of any size buys through) sit inside the ESTIMATED 1.A.2 industrial liquids - OCAC's Total Industry customer-class rows (src/pkinv/sectors/industry/data.py), which the transport fuel ledger excludes from the road control by construction (its RESOLVED-OBSERVED Industry claimant row). Only retail-pump captive diesel remains inside the 1.A.3.b Road control at road factors - the UNRESOLVED claimant row 'Captive generation (retail)' of outputs/transport\_fuel\_ledger\_2024.csv, declared as biasing road transport high. Captive GAS self-generation is a separate, estimated category (computed by the power module, reported under industry through data/stream\_reporting\_sector.csv); this row is its liquid-fuel sibling. See transport-hsd-end-use. \\[2pt]
1.A.2 & Construction and industrial mobile machinery (1A2gvii) & IE & CO2/\allowbreak CH4/\allowbreak N2O & IPCC books construction and industrial off-road machinery under 1.A.2 (gvii), NOT under 1.A.4.c - a mapping this inventory previously overgeneralised. The fuel is reported inside the Mixed off-road (1A4c/1A2) category, whose class is the source workbook's residual bucket as well as its tractor class, so whatever construction plant the residual contains is estimated there at Table 3.3.1 factors and allocated on a cropland proxy that is wrong for it. Splitting the residual needs equipment stock data no source here provides. \\[2pt]
2.F.1 & Mobile air-conditioning (road vehicles) & NE & HFC & Refrigerant leakage from vehicle air-conditioning is IPPU 2.F.1, not combustion, so it is outside the fuel anchor by construction - but it is a real transport-fleet emission this inventory does not yet report anywhere: the 2.F species-aware bank engine is implemented and the Ozone Secretariat's 2024 consumption control is loaded, but the mobile-air-conditioning application split has not been reconciled here. See transport-mobile-ac-hfc. \\[2pt]
(air) & Air pollutants - road transport & E & PM2.5/\allowbreak PM10/\allowbreak CO/\allowbreak NOx/\allowbreak NMVOC/\allowbreak SO2/\allowbreak NH3 & Per-kilometre factors on the same survival-weighted vehicle-kilometres that distribute the fuel control total. Unlike the greenhouse-gas side this layer does NOT inherit the fuel anchor, so its magnitude rides the fleet model. PROVENANCE FLAW, declared: the g/km factors are Punjab-workbook transcriptions with no primary citation located (emission\_factors\_gkm.csv has no provenance column), and the layer is exhaust-only - read it as order-of-magnitude. \\[2pt]
(air) & Air pollutants - road transport cold-start excess & NE & CO/\allowbreak NMVOC/\allowbreak NOx/\allowbreak PM2.5 & Excess emissions during engine warm-up are a separate EMEP/EEA process (2023 guidebook ch 1.A.3.b hot/cold methodology) requiring trip counts, trip lengths and ambient temperature on top of the hot-exhaust factors; none of those inputs has been assembled here. The exploratory diagnostic is hot-exhaust-only. See transport-cold-start. \\[2pt]
(air) & Air pollutants - road transport evaporative NMVOC & E & NMVOC & Estimated by the air program's Tier 1 refactor: the 1.A.3.b.v Gasoline evaporation chapter was acquired (sources/EMEP/) and its per-vehicle-day factors (20-35 C band) ride the fleet model's own active petrol counts as separate evaporative atoms in pkinv.sectors.transport.air\_pollutants. The year-round hottest-band assumption is the layer's declared limitation. Gap transport-evaporative-nmvoc is CLOSED. \\[2pt]
(air) & Air pollutants - road transport non-exhaust PM (tyre, brake and road\ldots & E & TSP/\allowbreak PM10/\allowbreak PM2.5 & Estimated by the air program's Tier 1 refactor: the 1.A.3.b.vi-vii chapters were acquired (sources/EMEP/) and their g/vkm factors ride the same survival-weighted vehicle-kilometres the fuel split rides, as separate tyre\_brake\_wear and road\_wear atoms - the coarser TSP/PM10 strata beside, never summed into, the PM2.5 core. Road-dust resuspension stays out. Gap transport-nonexhaust-pm is CLOSED. \\[2pt]
